name: Where AI Sits in the Global Risk Rankings
blurb:
The World Economic Forum published its Global Risks Report 2026 in February 2026. It asks respondents to rank the risks most likely to present a material crisis, across an immediate view, a two-year outlook and a ten-year outlook. The value of it for an AI reference site is not the AI commentary but the comparison: it puts AI risk next to armed conflict, extreme weather and inequality, and asks people to choose.

For 2026 specifically, Adverse outcomes of AI technologies entered the top ten for the first time, at number 8, selected by 4 percent of respondents. Cyber insecurity entered alongside it at number 9 on 3 percent. The report describes both as new entrants and notes an uptick in concern for technological risks entering 2026.

The more informative pattern is what happens as the horizon lengthens. Adverse outcomes of AI technologies ranks 5th over ten years, up one position from the previous year's ranking, and the report identifies it, with adverse outcomes of frontier technologies, as among the risks showing the largest increases in severity score between the two-year and ten-year outlooks. Misinformation and disinformation ranks 4th over ten years, also up one position.

So the picture is a risk that people do not expect to break this year and do expect to worsen considerably, which is a different profile from the risks above it. Geoeconomic confrontation leads the immediate ranking at 18 percent and then falls 19 positions to number 19 over ten years, the only risk respondents expected to improve.

points.desc: Adverse outcomes of AI technologies ranks 8th among risks most likely to present a material crisis on a global scale in 2026, selected by 4 percent of respondents. The report identifies it as a new entrant to the top ten, alongside cyber insecurity at 9th on 3 percent.
points.name: AI entered the immediate top ten for the first time

points.desc: Geoeconomic confrontation leads at 18 percent, state-based armed conflict at 14 percent, extreme weather events at 8 percent, societal polarization and misinformation and disinformation at 7 percent each, economic downturn at 5 percent, and erosion of human rights or civic freedoms at 4 percent. AI risk is real in this ranking and it is not the thing people expect to break first.
points.name: What outranks it in the immediate view

points.desc: Over a ten-year horizon, adverse outcomes of AI technologies ranks 5th and misinformation and disinformation 4th, each up one position from the previous year. The report names AI and frontier technologies among the risks showing the largest increases in severity score between the two-year and ten-year outlooks.
points.name: It ranks higher the further out you look

points.desc: The report expects progress in AI and quantum technologies to accelerate over the next decade with each fuelling breakthroughs in the other, and flags potentially cascading risk impacts, specifically in the context of rising geoeconomic confrontation. That links the technological ranking to the geopolitical one rather than treating them separately.
points.name: AI and quantum are treated as compounding each other

points.desc: Of the risks surveyed, geoeconomic confrontation is the single one respondents expected to get better, falling 18 positions from the two-year outlook to number 19 over ten years. Every technological risk moves the other way. That contrast is the report's most quotable finding for anyone arguing that AI risk is a near-term problem: the data says the opposite, and says it is worse for that.
points.name: One risk was expected to improve, and it is not a technological one

points.desc: The rankings come from a survey of respondents asked what they believe most likely to cause a crisis. That is a useful signal about where attention and policy pressure will go, and it is not an actuarial estimate. A risk can rise in this ranking because it became more salient rather than more likely.
points.name: What this measures is perception, not probability

summary: The World Economic Forum's Global Risks Report 2026 ranks what a global survey of respondents expects to cause a material crisis. AI entered the immediate top ten for the first time at number 8, and ranks higher the further out the horizon goes.
